children: New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Diwali 2026 Muhurat Trading Stocks: Investors preparing their portfolios for Samvat 2083 have six technical stock recommendations from HDFC Securities, with potential upside ranging from 19% to 28% over the period until the next Diwali. The brokerage's Muhurat Trading Technical Picks report identifies opportunities across the oil and gas, IT, financial services, steel and credit sectors.

Along with two price targets for each recommendation, it has specified entry ranges, average levels and closing-basis stop losses to help investors track the suggested trades. HDFC Securities also cautioned that its report should not be the sole basis for investment decisions. Here are the six recommendations and the technical factors behind them.
HDFC Securities has recommended BPCL in the Rs.304-315 range, with an average level of Rs.289. Its price targets are Rs.342 and Rs.366, while the closing-basis stop loss is Rs.274.

The brokerage's bullish view is supported by the stock's broad consolidation base between Rs.275 and Rs.330 since March. BPCL has broken above a falling channel that had been in place between August and October and has formed higher lows around Rs.277-280. An inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, with its head near Rs.277, has also completed a breakout above the Rs.296-300 neckline. The stock has moved above its 50-day exponential moving average, while weekly stochastic indicators have exited the oversold zone.

HDFC Securities said, "The Aug-Oct falling channel has been broken on the upside, with higher lows from 277-280. An inverse head and shoulders (head near 277) has formed since 8 Oct; today's close above the 296-300 neckline completes it."

The brokerage has recommended HCL Technologies in the Rs.1,405-1,440 entry range, with an average level of Rs.1,285. It has set price targets of Rs.1,580 and Rs.1,686, indicating a potential upside of 20%. The stop loss is Rs.1,250 on a closing basis.

The stock has broken out of an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern on the weekly chart, accompanied by higher trading volumes. HCL Tech has also moved above key moving-average resistance and sustained those levels. The brokerage noted that the Nifty IT index had broken above its long-term moving averages, providing a supportive sector trend. Momentum indicators remain positive, with the weekly MACD above its equilibrium and signal lines and the weekly RSI above 50.
HDFC Securities said, "Stock price has broken out from inverted head and shoulder pattern on the weekly chart. Price breakout is accompanied with jump in volumes on weekly charts."

IIFL Finance has an entry range of Rs.578-600 and an average level of Rs.535. HDFC Securities has set successive targets of Rs.670 and Rs.720, indicating a potential upside of 24%. The recommended closing-basis stop loss is Rs.510.

The brokerage's technical assessment points to a potential recovery after the stock corrected sharply from Rs.640 to Rs.513 and subsequently began building a base. Trading volumes have picked up, suggesting greater participation in the move. The stock has also formed a higher low and moved above its 21-day and 200-day moving averages, indicating an improvement in its short-term trend. The 14-week stochastic indicator has turned oversold, while a Doji candlestick pattern followed by buying during the current week adds to the possibility of a bullish reversal.

HDFC Securities has recommended JSW Steel in the Rs.1,340-1,383 range, with an average level of Rs.1,235. The brokerage has assigned targets of Rs.1,505 and Rs.1,600, indicating a potential upside of 19%. Its closing-basis stop loss is Rs.1,195.

The recommendation is supported by a breakout above a horizontal trend line on the weekly chart. The stock is trading above its 200-day exponential moving average and has been forming higher tops and higher bottoms, indicating a sustained upward trend. It is also positioned above key moving averages across time frames. The weekly RSI is above 50, while the MACD has moved back above the equilibrium line, suggesting positive momentum.

Satin Creditcare offers the highest potential upside among the six picks. HDFC Securities has suggested an entry range of Rs.256-265 and an average level of Rs.230. Its targets are Rs.300 and Rs.330, while the closing-basis stop loss is Rs.220.

The stock broke out of a prolonged consolidation range of Rs.130-180 in June 2026, supported by above-average volumes. The move was accompanied by a positive moving-average crossover, with the 20-week simple moving average crossing above the 50-week average. After moving higher, the stock corrected between July and September to test Rs.210. Its latest breakout from the recent range suggests the intermediate uptrend could resume. The 14-month RSI has also crossed 60, indicating strong momentum.

HDFC Securities said, "The breakout was accompanied with a positive MA crossover as the 20-week SMA moved above the 50-week SMA. The stock then gradually moved higher before pulling back in the months of July-September 2026 to test a low of 210."

HDFC Securities has recommended Zensar Technologies in the Rs.533-548 entry range, with an average level of Rs.495. The brokerage has set targets of Rs.615 and Rs.666, indicating a potential upside of 25%. The closing-basis stop loss is Rs.469.

The technical outlook is supported by a higher-bottom reversal pattern around Rs.416 in September. A strong bullish candle on the monthly chart in October indicated a possible end to the stock's downtrend. Zensar is also approaching the upper end of a broader consolidation range of Rs.425-550. The brokerage highlighted positive divergence in the 14-month RSI in September, which was subsequently confirmed by the stock's sharp upward move.
The six recommendations cover the period until the next Diwali.
